engagement_background.objective: Achieve $240K–$470K in cost savings across selected spend categories through a 6-month strategic sourcing program, while maintaining or improving service levels and leveraging SaVida Health’s enterprise purchasing power.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Ten indirect spend categories with a combined baseline of ~$5.3 M are in scope (EMR, Employee Benefits, Lab & Medical Supplies, Small Parcel, IT Hardware, Telecom, Office Supplies, Commercial Print, Waste Management). Some low-spend / low-opportunity categories may be dropped as the project progresses; direct clinical care outside these categories is out of scope.
constraints_challenges: Supplier lack of responsiveness to data requests
Incumbent supplier pushback and sensitivities during sourcing activities
Risk of uncontrolled “side conversations” with suppliers requiring a unified communication strategy
Limited stakeholder availability for data provision, interviews, and approvals
Need for rapid ‘quick-hit’ savings before year-end and full completion by March 2025
Gaps in internal line-item usage data, necessitating supplier data requests and potential data shortfalls
Requirement for SaVida to halt any parallel procurement activity in scoped categories
Aggressive overall 6-month timeline for sourcing, negotiations, and contracting

procurement_environment.data_availability: Basic AP/PO and contract files exist but detailed usage data often resides with suppliers; Treya must collect unit-level data and supplier-provided line-item histories.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: No centralized spend view; historical usage data incomplete and supplier participation needed. Both parties agree to proceed even if gaps remain after reasonable efforts.
